preamble: Insertion of the voiced dental fricative [ð] is rare. It occurs in Spanish through hypercorrection. Colloquial Spanish drops intervocalic /d/ in the participle ending -ado (cansado > cansao), so speakers who restore the d by hypercorrection add one to words that never had it, giving bacalado for bacalao and Bilbado for Bilbao. Phonemically the inserted segment is /d/, but Spanish /d/ is always [ð̞] between vowels, so the consonant that actually appears is the fricative; no stop stage ever surfaces.

examples.note: A nonstandard hypercorrect form in which -ao is taken for colloquial -ado. The from form is the standard pronunciation, which has no [ð].
